tickets.title: App: the filter and a full re-sort block the main thread on very large lists
tickets.description:
On 50,000 issues, one filter keystroke takes about 40 ms on the main thread. A live update that changes a title takes about 76 ms. At 10,000 issues these are about 10 ms and 22 ms. At 1,000 issues they fit in a frame. LLM-105 has the full table.

The cost is the filter, the sort and the rebuilt rows, all done on the main thread. The fix is to run them on a background task and apply the result when it is ready. That needs a rule for the selection while a result is on its way, so I did not do it in LLM-105.

The owner's tracker holds 113 issues today, so this only matters if a tracker grows past about 10,000 issues.

+++ Agent notes
Estimate: 45 minutes, $12. I set it before the claim.

Landed in b8e094e on main.

- `issues/rows.rs` holds the build: filter, sort and groups as one pure function. The list calls it through `IssueList::recompute`.
- From 2,000 issues the build runs on a background task, on a snapshot of the store. Below that it runs on the main thread, as before.
- The store now holds each issue in an `Arc`. A snapshot costs one counter bump per issue.
- A newer build cancels an older one. A generation counter guards the result as well, so a stale result never lands.
- Selection rule: the list reads the selected row when the result lands, so a `j` pressed meanwhile counts. It keeps the issue by its ID. A filter keystroke still selects the first match, even when a live update arrives before its result.
- While a build is on its way, the list shows the old rows.

Threshold, from `row_build_times` in `shell/perf_tests.rs`, in a debug build. The machine had a load of about 30 to 60 from other builds.

| Issues | Keystroke build | Status groups build |
|---|---|---|
| 1,000 | 0.3 ms | 0.9 ms |
| 2,000 | 0.8 ms | 1.8 ms |
| 4,000 | 1.4 ms | 5 to 8 ms |
| 10,000 | 4 ms | 18 ms |
| 50,000 | 23 ms | 116 ms |

At 4,000 issues, the build grouped by status takes most of an 8 ms frame, so I set the threshold at 2,000.

Main-thread time per step, from the frame tests, in one run. "Main" sets `LLMTODO_PERF_MAIN_THREAD=1`, which keeps every build on the main thread.

| Step | 10k background | 10k main | 50k background | 50k main |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frame, nothing changed | 7.4 ms | 7.1 ms | 12.9 ms | 18.0 ms |
| Filter keystroke | 13.9 ms | 25.6 ms | 17.0 ms | 99.3 ms |
| Live update, new title | 18.0 ms | 29.5 ms | 31.3 ms | 91.2 ms |
| Keystroke until result landed | 39.7 ms | 22.9 ms | 110 ms | 93 ms |

On the background path, a keystroke costs about one plain frame. The last row is the whole cost, because the test executor runs the background task on the same thread.

Not done: a live title update at 50,000 issues still costs about 31 ms. A new description costs the same, so the rest is outside the list.

Tests: `cargo test -p llmtodo-app` passed, 366 tests. That run includes the 6 new tests in `issues/background_tests.rs` and the LLM-144 scroll tests. Clippy with `-D warnings` and fmt are clean.

Found on the way: a claim moved this Todo ticket to User review. LLM-150 tracks it. I set In Progress by hand, then claimed.
+++

tickets.title: App: add a GPU frame benchmark in its own package
tickets.description:
The timings in LLM-105 come from headless test windows. They cover state updates, layout and scene building. They leave out text rasterizing and presenting, so they are not real frame times.

GPUI's `#[gpui::bench]` draws through headless Metal and reports real frame data. It must not run with GPUI's `test-support` feature. `crates/app` enables that feature in its dev-dependencies, so the benchmark needs a separate package that shares the app's views. That means splitting part of the app into a library crate, which is larger than a performance fix.

+++ Agent notes
Landed on `main` in three commits:

- `a316d38` moves the views, the model, the assets and `build.rs` into a new library crate, `crates/ui` (`llmtodo-ui`). The files moved unchanged, so git keeps their history.
- `e9d0c2d` points the scripts and the docs at the new paths.
- `0a1dab8` adds `crates/ui-bench` (`llmtodo-ui-bench`), the benchmarks, a CI check and the perf section in `SPEC.md`.

The binary in `crates/app` holds only `main.rs` and start-up. The menus stayed in `llmtodo-ui`: `Workspace` handles the menu actions, and the tests call `llmtodo_ui::init`, which binds them. App tests now run with `cargo test -p llmtodo-ui`.

`llmtodo-ui` has a `bench-support` feature. It only turns on the demo data module. The bench package turns on GPUI's `bench-support` through `gpui-pre` and `gpui-pre-platform`, at the same version GPUI Kit pins, so no second GPUI copy builds. `cargo tree` shows no `test-support` in its feature graph, and a new CI step fails when one appears.

Run: `cargo bench -p llmtodo-ui-bench --bench task_list`. Window 1400 by 900. Three other agents built at the same time, so the worst frames are noisy.

| Benchmark | Issues | Time per step | Draw p50 | Draw p99 | Draw max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Scroll | 1,000 | 3.7 ms | 3.4 ms | 5.3 ms | 8.3 ms |
| Scroll | 10,000 | 4.0 ms | 3.7 ms | 5.8 ms | 22.9 ms |
| Scroll | 50,000 | 4.9 ms | 4.4 ms | 7.9 ms | 25.8 ms |
| Filter keystroke | 1,000 | 7.3 ms | 5.3 ms | 21.1 ms | 82.9 ms |
| Filter keystroke | 10,000 | 5.4 ms | 4.2 ms | 15.7 ms | 27.7 ms |
| Filter keystroke | 50,000 | 6.5 ms | 5.3 ms | 12.0 ms | 16.5 ms |
| First draw | 1,000 | 16.2 ms | 6.7 ms | 18.0 ms | 26.7 ms |
| First draw | 10,000 | 17.0 ms | 5.7 ms | 17.1 ms | 28.4 ms |
| First draw | 50,000 | 21.6 ms | 8.4 ms | 28.2 ms | 49.7 ms |

Limits:

- The benchmark app has no asset source, because `BenchAppContext` cannot take one. So the icons draw nothing.
- The 1,000 issue filter is the slowest keystroke. Lists below 2,000 issues build their rows on the main thread.

Checks: clippy with warnings as errors and fmt pass. `llmtodo-ui` tests pass, 368 of them. `scripts/bundle-macos` builds `llmtodo-app` with the HardHat icon, and the binary carries the same commit stamp as the bundle. I did not run `scripts/publish`.

tickets.title: Contract: Endpoint trait, Change<T>, typed activity events, ID newtypes
tickets.description:
Finding 4 of LLM-122, step 3 of its suggested order.

- Add an Endpoint trait with the method, path, request, response and whether it writes. Generate the route table from it. The client gets one generic call.
- Add Change<T> with Keep, Clear and Set. It replaces the empty-string convention in UpdateIssue. waiting_on becomes the enum on the wire.

- 4922178: `Endpoint` trait in `api_types::routes`, with one type per endpoint in `ep`. `ROUTES` is generated from them. The server mounts handlers by endpoint type. tickets.title: CLI: llmtodo init for a repo, and a global skill that runs it
tickets.description:
The owner asked for this on 2026-11-11. They want a simple way to set up llmtodo in any new project, by hand or through an LLM.

Today neither part exists. There is no `llmtodo init` command. The `llmtodo` skill lives only in this repo, in `.claude/skills/llmtodo`, so agents in other repos do not have it.

## What to build

- `llmtodo init` writes `.llmtodo.toml` at the git root with the team and project. It offers existing teams and projects, or creates new ones. It also works with flags and `--no-input`, so an agent can run it.
- Running it again does not overwrite an existing file unless asked.
- A global skill in `~/.claude/skills`, installed by a repo script or by `llmtodo init`, teaches any agent how to use the tracker and how to run `llmtodo init` in a repo that has no `.llmtodo.toml`.
- The global skill and the repo skill must not drift apart. Generate one from the other, or make the repo skill point to the global one.
- The skill must not depend on files that exist only in this repo, such as `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.

+++ Agent notes
Landed in 047c64a.

- `llmtodo init` writes `.llmtodo.toml` at the git root. Flags: `--team`, `--team-name`, `--project`, `--project-name`, `--create`, `--force`, `--no-skill`. Without a terminal it never asks. A missing value exits with code 8, and a missing team or project without `--create` exits with code 2.
- Running it again with the same values or no values changes nothing. Other values need `--force`. A replaced file keeps its `actor` line.
- `llmtodo skill install`, `skill status` and `skill print` handle `~/.claude/skills/llmtodo`, or `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/skills/llmtodo`. `init` installs the skill too.
- The binary embeds `.claude/skills/llmtodo/SKILL.md` and `guide.md`, so the repo skill and the global skill are one source. A test checks that they match and that the skill does not point at `docs/agents`.
- A manifest `.llmtodo-skill.json` records a hash of each file the command wrote. A file with another hash, or a linked folder, is kept. `--force` renames it to `<name>.bak-<seconds>` first.
- The generic guide moved from `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` to the skill's `guide.md`. The doc keeps only the publish steps for this repo.
- `scripts/publish` does not install the skill. The owner runs `llmtodo skill install` once after the next publish.
+++

+++ Review
### Steps to reproduce
1. Publish this round.
2. Make an empty folder and run git init in it.
3. In that folder, run: llmtodo init
4. Pick a team and a project when it asks.
5. Run: llmtodo init again.
6. Answer N when it asks to replace the file.
7. Run: llmtodo skill status

### What to check
- The folder now has a .llmtodo.toml file with your team and project.
- The second llmtodo init shows changed: false.
- skill status shows current for SKILL.md and guide.md.
- The skill is in ~/.claude/skills/llmtodo.
+++

tickets.title: Server: any review status ends the claim, not only User review

tickets.title: Pixel cat mascot in the sidebar
tickets.description:
Add the pixel cat mascot to the app. It sits at the bottom left of the left sidebar.

The art is final. It lives in `design/mascot/`. Open `design/mascot/preview.html` to see it.

## Behaviour

- An agent session is active: the cat works on its laptop.
- Nothing is going on: the cat sleeps.
- Hover or click the cat: it sits and watches for a while. Then it walks or sleeps, picked at random. After that it goes back to the rule above.

## Colours

- Light theme: black cat, the "Soft" palette.
- Dark theme: white cat, the "Pure white" palette.

+++ Agent notes


### Round 1

Landed on `main` in `ac2843a` and published.

- `design/mascot/export.mjs --app` writes `crates/ui/assets/mascot/mascot.json`. `design/mascot/README.md` says how to run it again.
- `crates/ui/src/shell/mascot/`: `sprites.rs` parses the art once, `behaviour.rs` holds the rules with no GPUI, and `mod.rs` is the view.
- I paint each run of one colour as one quad on a canvas, snapped to device pixels, so the cat stays sharp at any zoom.
- The cat is a sibling of the sidebar, and the workspace draws the sidebar as a cached view. Without that, each cat frame redrew the sidebar's issue counts, about 12 ms at 10k issues. Now one cat frame costs about 4 to 5 ms.

### Round 2

Landed on `main` in `40f28dc` and published. These are the owner's changes from chat.

- The cat has no hover or pressed style. The owner made this the one exception to the hover rule.
- At work, a hover or a single click changes nothing. A double click walks the cat to the other side, where it works again. A double click on the way turns it around. Only the second click of a run counts, so a triple click turns it once.
- When work ends away from the left edge, the cat walks home. Then it sleeps, or it sits and watches for 4 to 8 s and then sleeps. A coin flip picks which. If work ends on the way right, it turns for home.
- A new session starts on the left: the cat works there. A session that starts on the way home: it works when it gets home.
- Each time the sidebar opens, the start of the app too, the cat waits out of view for 1 to 3 s. Then it walks in to its spot: the left edge, or the right edge if it works there. The strip is now as wide as the sidebar and clips the cat at its edge. A 2-pixel inset keeps the resting cat off the edge.
- Hiding the sidebar stops the timer. The next open starts the walk-in again. Hover and clicks do nothing during the wait or the walk-in. Claims that change meanwhile decide where it ends: at work or asleep.
- During any walk to a side, hover and single clicks do nothing.
- Tests: 29 mascot tests, all on the test clock. They include the walk-in being cancelled by a hide. `cargo test -p llmtodo-ui` passes 421.

### Round 3

Landed on `main` in `1836039` and published. These are the owner's changes after round 2.

- While the mouse button is down on the cat, it draws at 98% size around the bottom centre, so its feet stay on the ground. It goes back to full size on release, wherever the release lands. This works in every state.

The edges stay sharp, and runs that touch share an edge, so no gaps or blurred seams show. A few sprite pixels come out one device pixel narrower. The other choice was fractional edges, which blur every edge and show faint seams between runs. `quads()` in `mascot/mod.rs` holds the geometry, and two tests check it.
- Every click during any walk is ignored: the walk-in, a walk to a side, the walk home and a roaming walk. A double click starts a new walk only once the cat works at its spot. I dropped the round 2 rule that a double click turns the cat around.
- Tests: 34 mascot tests. One sends double clicks on every frame of a walk, and the cat still reaches the far side. `cargo test -p llmtodo-ui` passes 426.

Landed on `main` in `a6bdd85` and published.

- The owner decided that a hover must not stop a roaming walk. Now no walk of any kind stops for a hover or a click.
- A hover still makes a sleeping, napping or sitting idle cat sit and watch.
- A pointer still on the cat when a walk ends does nothing until it leaves and comes back. It does not hold a cat that sits after the walk home, either. `hold` in `behaviour.rs` tracks this.
- Tests: 3 new state machine tests, for a hover during a roaming walk, a pointer left on the cat after the walk home, and a hover on a napping cat. `cargo test -p llmtodo-ui` passes 429.
+++

Found in the 2026-11-12 performance review. I checked each point against the code and the GPUI source.

## Cause

- In GPUI, `cx.notify()` on a view marks that view and every ancestor dirty (`zed/crates/gpui/src/window.rs:2479` `mark_view_dirty`). The root always renders again. A child view renders again unless it is drawn with `.cached(..)`.
- Only the sidebar is cached (`crates/ui/src/shell/workspace/render.rs:191`). `render_split` adds `self.list` and `self.task` uncached (`render.rs:124`, `:132`). The inbox, settings and document views are uncached too.
- The cat timer notifies on every step: 90 ms walk and laptop, 120 ms watch, 160 ms sleep (`crates/ui/src/shell/mascot/mod.rs:158-181`). So `Workspace`, the list and the task view render 6 to 11 times a second all day. The comment at `render.rs:174-177` assumes the cat frame does not reach the list. It does, through `Workspace`.
- The reviewer ran `frame_times_10k` from `perf_tests.rs`: one cat frame takes 15.0 ms median, and a full frame takes 17.2 ms.
- The update button uses `with_animation(.., Animation::new(GRADIENT_TURN).repeat(), ..)` (`crates/ui/src/shell/workspace/update.rs:212-218`). Each animation frame calls `window.request_animation_frame()`, which notifies the current view (`window.rs:2942`). That view is `Workspace`, so the whole window renders at the display rate, 60 or 120 Hz, while an update waits. `scripts/publish` makes this state common.
- The cat timer keeps waking the main thread while the window is hidden or minimized.

## Fix

1. Draw `self.list`, `self.task`, `self.inbox`, `self.settings_view` and `self.doc_view` with `.cached(StyleRefinement::default().size_full())`, as the sidebar does. Check that each view notifies itself on every change it shows. Watch for state that `Workspace` passes in during render and that would go stale under caching.
2. Move the update button into its own small view, so its animation notifies only that view.
3. Stop the cat timer while the window is not visible (`window.observe_window_visibility`). Restart it when the window shows again.
4. Add a test that counts `IssueList::render` and `TaskView::render` calls across one `mascot.tick` and across one update-button frame. Both counts must be zero.
5. Remeasure with `perf_tests.rs` and put the numbers here.

The status bar count fix in LLM-174 helps here too, but it is not needed for this one.


## What I changed

Commit `460324e` on main.

- The list, task, inbox, settings and document views are drawn with `.cached(size_full)`, as the sidebar is.
- Each of them now observes the store. The task view and the inbox also observe `AnswerInputs`, which notifies when a feedback field must clear.
- `list_do` notifies the list, so the closures that set list fields directly stay correct. The other direct writes from the workspace notify too.
- A cached view is laid out as its own root, where `flex_1` does nothing. The roots of the list, inbox, settings and document views now use `size_full`. Without that, the list measured itself too narrow and hid columns. Existing tests caught this.
- The update button is its own view, `UpdateButton`. The workspace copies its state into it, and a click emits `RestartClicked`.
- The cat pauses while the window is hidden (`observe_window_visibility`). It goes on from where it was, with no walk-in.
- New tests in `shell/cache_tests.rs` count renders with `render_count`. They check that a cat frame and an update-button frame draw neither the list nor the task view. They also check that store changes and workspace changes still draw every cached view. I removed the observers on purpose once, and the tests failed.

## Numbers

`frame_times_10k`, debug build, on a busy machine:

- Cat frame: 2.8 ms median. A full frame takes 18 ms in the same run, and before this change a cat frame drew the same views as a full frame.
- The old "mascot frame" line used `render_frame`, which refreshes the whole window. So it always measured a full frame (43 ms in my baseline run). It now uses a plain `window.draw`, as the platform does.

The workspace still renders on each cat frame and each update-button frame. GPUI marks every ancestor of a notified view dirty, so this cannot be avoided. The status bar work in it is the part LLM-174 made cheaper.
+++

tickets.title: App: the $EDITOR check never stops and redraws the window every 400 ms
tickets.description:
After the owner opens a description in `$EDITOR` once, the app redraws the whole window every 400 ms until it quits. The check for saved files never stops.

It also blocks two features. Tracker switching and "Restart to update" both refuse while an `$EDITOR` edit is open, and in practice an edit never closes.

+++ Agent notes


Found in the 2026-11-12 performance review. Confirmed in the code.

## Cause

- `start_external_poll` (`crates/ui/src/shell/workspace.rs:3477`) starts a 400 ms loop. Nothing ever sets `_external_poll` back to `None`.
- `poll_external` (`workspace.rs:3493`) calls `cx.notify()` on every tick, even when `self.external.poll()` returned no saves.
- `ExternalEdits::poll` (`crates/ui/src/model/external_editor.rs:234`) ends a session only when its temp file is gone. No code deletes `llmtodo-edit/<KEY>.md`, so sessions never end.
- Each tick runs one `stat` per session on the main thread.
- Tracker switching (`workspace.rs:672`) and restart (`workspace/update.rs:124`) refuse while `external.is_empty()` is false.

## Fix

1. Call `cx.notify()` only when the poll returned saves or a session ended.
2. Stop the loop when `self.external.is_empty()` after a poll. Start it again on the next `$EDITOR` open.
3. End a session when the editor process exits, or when its task closes or is deleted. Delete the temp file when the session ends. The launcher may not give a process handle for every editor. Check `Launcher` and pick the simplest signal that works for both terminal and GUI editors.
4. Add tests: no notify on an idle tick, the loop stops when the last session ends, and a session ends when the editor exits.

## What I changed

Commit `5cc8473` on main.

- The launcher gives no process handle: Terminal and terminal multiplexers run the command themselves. So the shell line is now `<editor> '<file>'; touch '<file>.done'`. This works for terminal editors and for GUI editors that wait, such as `code --wait`.
- On the next check after the marker appears, the app reads the file one last time and saves it. Then it ends the session and deletes the file and the marker.
- A session also ends when its file is gone, or when its task goes to the Trash or leaves the store. I did not end sessions when a task closes, because editing a Done task's description is a real use. This is my default; say if you want closed tasks to end edits too.
- An editor that returns within 3 s did not wait, such as `code` without `--wait`. Its session stays open for saves, and the status bar tells the owner to set EDITOR to wait.
- `poll_external` notifies only when it found a save, an end or a detached editor. The 400 ms loop stops when the last session ends, and the next `Shift+E` starts it again.
- A new open deletes an old marker for the same task first.
- Tests cover an idle poll, the last save before an exit, a quick exit, the task leaving, a gone file, an old marker, no notify on idle ticks, and the loop stopping.
+++

+++ Review
### Steps to reproduce
1. Open any task you can edit.
2. Press Shift+E.
3. Change the text in the editor and save it.
4. Quit the editor.
5. Switch to another tracker.

### What to check
- After you save, the task shows the new text.
- After you quit, the status bar says "Closed <key> in $EDITOR".
- Switching the tracker works. It no longer says to close $EDITOR first.
+++

tickets.title: App: every live event fetches the full issue and runs git for each touched issue
tickets.description:
Every live event fetches the full detail of each issue it touches, and runs git for it. This happens for every issue, not only the open one. Busy agents send many events, so the app and the server do a lot of wasted work.

Make a live refresh fetch only what the list needs. Fetch the full detail and run git only for the task the panel shows.

+++ Agent notes


Found in the 2026-11-12 performance review. Confirmed in the code.

## Cause

- `flush` (`crates/ui/src/model/backend.rs:797-800`) calls `refresh` for each touched key, one after another.
- `refresh` (`backend.rs:1011`) calls `client.issue(key)`. The server builds a full `IssueDetail` with about 35 queries (`crates/server/src/store/issue_detail.rs:10`): description, all comments, sessions, attachments, reviews, relations. The app keeps only the issue, relations, reviews and git panel.
- `send_issue_and_git` (`backend.rs:962`) then runs `with_commits`. `fill_commits` (`crates/client/src/git.rs:283-322`) spawns git processes: `git log`, `git reflog show` and `git rev-list` per local session, and always `git remote get-url origin` when no session gave a URL. The app shows git only for the open task (`crates/ui/src/task/task_view.rs:462`).
- One refresh sends four events: `Issue`, `Relations`, `Reviews` and `Git`. Each one updates the store, and each store update runs at least six observers (`workspace.rs:425-462`, `sidebar.rs:113`, `inbox/mod.rs:469`, `mascot/mod.rs:80`).
- The workspace applies one backend event per `this.update` (`workspace.rs:619-628`). So a burst of events runs the store observers once per event. Two observers scan every issue.
- With a saved view open, each issue change refetches the whole view through `query_all` with full issue objects and keeps only the IDs (`workspace.rs:2250-2267`, `backend.rs:907-925`).

## Fix

1. Server and client: add a `keys` (or `ids`) filter to `IssueQuery`. Refresh the touched list rows with one query.
2. Fetch the full detail only for the open task. Run `fill_commits` only for it.
3. Cache the `origin` URL per repo folder.
4. Send one event per refresh, such as `Event::IssueDetail { issue, relations, reviews, git }`, and apply it in one store update.
5. Drain the events that already wait (`try_next`) inside one `update`, so the observers run once per batch.
6. For saved views: ask the server for IDs only, or match the changed issue against the view's filter on the client.
7. Add a test that a live event on an issue that is not open makes no detail request and no git run.

LLM-172 and LLM-179 build on this change.

## What I changed

Commit `ca172be`.

- `IssueQuery` has a `keys` filter. Unknown keys are skipped. The CLI has `issue list --key`.
- A live refresh asks for all touched rows at once: one live query and one trash query, with text. Before, it made one full detail request per key, at about 35 queries each.
- Only the open task gets the full detail and a git run. The app tells the API thread which task is open with `Request::Open`. A write on another task sends back its row only.
- `Event::IssueDetail` carries the issue, relations, reviews and git panel. It replaces four events, so one refresh is one store update.
- The workspace applies every waiting event in one update. GPUI merges the store notifies, so observers run once per burst.
- `fill_commits` reads the `origin` URL through a 60 second cache per repo folder.
- A list copy marks the cached detail of that task as old. When the task opens again, the app fetches its detail once.
- Tests: the server keys query, the origin cache, the stale-detail store rule, and a live test that a non-open task gets a list copy and the open task gets its detail.

Not done: item 6, the saved view refresh. It still loads issue rows without text to read their IDs. A list of IDs only would need a new route and a CLI command. The refresh already waits 250 ms for issues to stop changing.
+++

tickets.title: App: the owner's writes wait behind live refreshes
tickets.description:
The owner's writes can wait behind live refreshes. The backend handles one thing at a time. While it refreshes many issues, a status change from the owner sits in the queue, so the server sees it late.

A steady stream of live events can also delay the refresh itself without end.

+++ Agent notes


Found in the 2026-11-12 performance review.

## Cause

- The session loop (`crates/ui/src/model/backend.rs:556-683`) awaits each request in turn. A `flush` of N keys runs N HTTP fetches plus N git runs before it reads the next request. `History` does the same inline (`backend.rs:621-636`).
- The settle timer is a new 40 ms `sleep` on every pass (`backend.rs:556-560`, `:679-681`). Any event or request restarts it. Events less than 40 ms apart keep `flush` from running, so the list goes stale.

## Fix

1. Handle writes first, for example with a `biased` select. Or run refreshes and history on spawned tasks with a small limit on how many run at once.
2. Start the settle deadline when `pending` first turns non-empty, and do not reset it.
3. Add tests: a write sent during a long flush reaches the server before the flush ends, and a steady event stream still flushes within the deadline.

LLM-171 makes each refresh much cheaper, so do it first.

## What I changed

Commit `c1ff0ed`.

- A live refresh runs on its own tokio task, one at a time. The session loop keeps reading requests while it runs, so a write goes out at once.
- The loop uses a `biased` select, so the owner's requests come before live events and refreshes.
- `History` runs on its own task too.
- The settle deadline starts when the first event arrives and does not move. A steady stream of events still gets a refresh within 40 ms of the first one.
- When a session ends during a refresh, the refresh's work goes back into the queue, so the next connect does it.
- Tests: a write during a 3 second refresh gets its answer first, and a stream of events 5 ms apart still gets a refresh in under 1 second. `Target` has a test-only `slow_flush` field for the first test.
+++

tickets.title: App: the description editor reparses the whole text on every keystroke
tickets.description:
The description editor parses the whole description again on every keystroke, on the main thread. Typing in a long description gets slow.

Make the editor parse only the changed part, with a time limit, as GPUI Kit's own highlighter does.

+++ Agent notes


Found in the 2026-11-12 performance review. Confirmed in the code.

## Cause

- `SectionFoldHighlighter::update` (`crates/ui/src/task/fold_highlighter.rs:69`) calls `self.inner.update(None, text, None)` and drops the edit. The code comment there already says the real app should pass the edit through.
- In GPUI Kit, a `None` edit means "change unknown", so tree-sitter reparses the whole text and all inline Markdown injections (`gpui-component/crates/component/src/highlighter/highlighter.rs:625-688`). The last `None` removes the time limit.
- With folding on, `fold_ranges(&text.to_string())` copies the whole rope on every keystroke (`fold_highlighter.rs:76`, `:92`).
- GPUI Kit's `TreeSitterInputHighlighter` (`input_adapter.rs:145-164`) passes the edit, uses a 2 ms limit, and parses texts over 256 KB in the background. Our wrapper replaces it and loses all three.
- The task view and the document view both use this highlighter.

## Fix

1. Convert the `InputEdit` to a tree-sitter edit and pass it to `update`. Copy the conversion from GPUI Kit's adapter; it is Apache-2.0, so add the source header.
2. Pass `Some(Duration::from_millis(2))` as the limit, and follow the adapter's background path for large texts.
3. Compute fold ranges from the rope line by line, without `to_string()`. Or recompute them only when the edit touches a `+++` line.
4. Add a test or benchmark that types into a long description, about 50 KB, and checks the time per key.

## What I changed

Commit `3c04013` on main.

- `SectionFoldHighlighter` converts each `InputEdit` to a tree-sitter edit and passes it to `SyntaxHighlighter::update`, with a 2 ms limit. It also handles batched edits with one parse. I copied `to_tree_sitter_edit` from GPUI Kit's adapter, with the source header.
- GPUI Kit's background-parse helpers are private. So when a parse times out, or the text is over 256 KB, the highlighter waits 150 ms for typing to pause. Then it parses a fresh `SyntaxHighlighter` on a background thread and swaps it in, unless a newer edit came meanwhile.
- Fold ranges come from the rope line by line. A new `Kind::of` reads each line's first characters, so no keystroke copies the text. Tests check that it matches the old rules on every edge case, and that the rope scan matches the text scan.
- The crate now depends on `tree-sitter =0.26.13` directly, the version GPUI Kit uses, for the edit type.
- New tests: the folds follow a typed line, and an ignored timing test, `typing_into_a_long_description`.

## Numbers

One typed key in a 50 KB description, with one frame, debug build: 165 ms median before, 34 ms after. The worst key went from 279 ms to 94 ms. The 34 ms that remain are the editor's own layout and render work, not parsing.
+++

tickets.title: App: the task view, document view and status bar redo text work on every render
tickets.description:
Some views redo the same text work on every render, and scrolling causes a render on every frame. The task view rebuilds its tabs and preview text, the document view copies its body, and the status bar builds a sorted list only to count it.

Cache this work and rebuild it only when its input changes.

+++ Agent notes
Found in the 2026-11-12 performance review.

## Cause

- Task view (`crates/ui/src/task/task_view.rs:300-343`, `:1086`, `:1119`, `:1153`, `:1815`): on each render, `open_tab` splits the description into new `String`s and clones the Activity and Sessions Markdown. `preview::prepare` rewrites each shown tab. `llmtodo_core::questions` parses the description twice, in `render` and in `tab_body`.
- `IssueStore::by_key` (`crates/ui/src/model/store.rs:234`) scans every issue. `preview::prepare` calls it for each issue key in the text, and `dependency_row` (`task_view.rs:747`) once per dependency.
- Document view (`crates/ui/src/docs/mod.rs:254`, `:266-268`): `render` clones the body and runs `preview::prepare` on it.
- GPUI notifies the view on each scroll-wheel event (`zed/crates/gpui/src/elements/div.rs:3441`), so all of this runs on every scroll frame. The Markdown parse itself is cached by `TextView`; only the string work repeats.
- Status bar (`crates/ui/src/shell/workspace/render.rs:430`): `claim_rows(store).len()` scans every issue, clones each claim with its key and title, and sorts them, only to show a count. It runs on every `Workspace` render.
- Settings (`crates/ui/src/settings/view.rs:400-407`): `hidden_count` scans the store on each render. It renders rarely, so this one is small.
- Conflict view (`task_view.rs:1294-1312`): builds a `HashSet` and a `SharedString` per line on each render while a conflict shows.

## Fix

1. Add a key-to-ID map to `IssueStore`, so `by_key` is a lookup.
2. Cache the prepared tabs on `TaskView`. Key the cache by issue ID, description version, history revision and a store counter that changes when the set of keys changes.
3. Store the prepared document text in `DocView::set_doc`, and rebuild it with the same key rule.
4. Keep a claim count in `IssueStore`, next to the open question count, and show that in the status bar.
5. Cache the conflict lines per conflict.

## What I changed

Commit `ad76c66`.

- `IssueStore` keeps a key-to-ID map, so `by_key` is one lookup. A `keys_revision` counter changes only when the set of keys changes. A snapshot with the same keys keeps it.
- `IssueStore` keeps the claim count and the open question count on every write. The status bar reads `claim_count()`, and the sidebar's question count no longer scans.
- `TaskView` caches its tabs, each tab's prepared Markdown and the parsed questions. The cache key is the issue ID, the description text, a history revision, the store's key revision and the server address. `render`, `open_tab` and `tab_body` all read the cache. `open_tab` now returns `Rc<Vec<Tab>>`.
- `activity` and `sessions` are private now. The workspace sets them with `TaskView::set_history`, which bumps the history revision.
- `DocView` keeps its prepared body until `set_doc`, `show` or `close`, or until the key revision or server address changes. `doc` is private, with a `doc()` reader.
- The conflict view caches its lines while neither text changes.
- I left the settings `hidden_count` as it is. It depends on the clock and renders rarely.
- Tests in `crates/ui/src/task/prepared_tests.rs`: five scroll frames build nothing, and new text, a new key and new history each build once. Two store tests check the key map and the claim count after every kind of write.
+++

tickets.title: App: the inbox never releases its answer and feedback fields
tickets.description:
The inbox keeps an input field for every question it ever showed, and a feedback field for every review ticket it ever showed. It never removes them, so they pile up over a long session. Key handling loops over all of them, so it slows down too.

+++ Agent notes
Found in the 2026-11-12 performance review.

## Cause

- `AnswerInputs.inputs` (`crates/ui/src/inbox/mod.rs:129-131`, `:186`) keeps one `InputState` entity and one `Subscription` per question ever drawn.
- `AnswerInputs.feedback` (`inbox/mod.rs:197-207`) keeps one `TextareaState` per review ticket ever opened.
- Nothing removes entries for answered questions or closed and deleted tasks.
- `AnswerInputs::focused` loops over every entry. The workspace calls it while it handles keys (`crates/ui/src/shell/workspace.rs:1674`, `:2668`, `:2992`).
- The inbox also rebuilds every card on every store change and clones every open `Question` in `entries()` (`inbox/mod.rs:469`, `:515-611`, `:672-680`). That is fine at today's counts.

## Fix

1. When the store's questions change, drop input entries whose question is no longer open. Keep an entry that has focus or unsent text.
2. Drop a feedback field when its ticket leaves the review status, unless it holds unsent text.
3. Add a test that the maps shrink after a question is answered and a review ticket is approved.

## What I changed

Commit `ba49e70`.

- `AnswerInputs` observes the store. On each change, `prune` drops the answer fields of questions that are no longer open in the store. It drops the feedback fields of tickets that left the review status, went to the Trash or left the store.
- A field with focus, or with text that is not only spaces, stays. The views make a field again when they draw it.
- `AnswerInputs::new` now takes the store and the window, so the workspace passes them.
- I left the inbox's card rebuild alone, as the review notes say it is fine at today's counts.
- Test: `answered_and_approved_fields_are_dropped` in `inbox/tests.rs`. It answers a question, moves a ticket out of review, and checks that a field with text stays until the text is gone.
+++

tickets.title: App: before the first connect, the app retries 4 times a second forever
tickets.description:
When the app cannot reach a server at start, it retries 4 times a second forever. It redraws the window on each retry. This happens, for example, when no server binary is installed.

+++ Agent notes


Found in the 2026-11-12 performance review. Confirmed in the code.

## Cause

- `Backoff::next` (`crates/ui/src/model/backend.rs:382-391`) doubles the delay only after a first connect. Before that, every retry waits `FIRST_DELAY`, 250 ms.
- Each retry reads `server.json`, makes a health request and sends `Event::Offline` (`backend.rs:397-408`). The app turns each one into a message change, `set_connection` and `cx.notify()`.

## Fix

1. Keep the fast retries for the first few seconds only, so a server that is still starting is found quickly. Then back off to `MAX_DELAY`.
2. Send `Offline` only when the reason changes.
3. Extend the existing backoff tests with the never-connected case.

## What I changed

Commit `f2a26bc`.

- Before the first connect, the first 12 retries wait 250 ms, so a starting server is found within about 3 seconds. After that, the wait doubles up to 5 seconds and stays there.
- Numbers with no server: before, 4 tries a second forever. After, 12 tries in the first 3 seconds, then about 5 more by 15 seconds, then one try every 5 seconds.
- The API thread sends `Offline` only when the reason changes, or for the first failure after a connect. Before, every try sent one and redrew the window.
- Tests: the backoff in the never-connected case, and the offline reason sent once.
+++

tickets.title: App: small leaks and waste in the data layer
tickets.description:
Small leaks and waste in the app's data layer. None is urgent on its own. Together they cost memory, allocations and main-thread time over a long session.

+++ Agent notes


Found in the 2026-11-12 performance review.

1. **The client parses every JSON response twice.** `raw_within` (`crates/client/src/lib.rs:360-372`, also `:299-310`, `:412-416`) reads the body as text, builds a `serde_json::Value`, then converts it with `from_value`. Deserialize the target type straight from the bytes on success. Parse `ErrorBody` only for status 400 and above.
2. **Per-issue caches are never pruned.** `replace_all` (`crates/ui/src/model/store.rs:273-284`) prunes `questions` but not `git`, `relations` or `reviews`. Entries stay after a purge and after a tracker switch. Run `retain` on all four maps.
3. **`WritePipeline::sent_keys` only grows** (`crates/ui/src/model/pipeline.rs:115-118`, `:150-163`). Remove the entry when `in_flight` for that ID reaches zero.
4. **`DraftStore` fsyncs on the main thread** (`crates/ui/src/model/drafts.rs:74-96`, `:101-116`). Each insert or remove rewrites `drafts.json` with `sync_all`. Write it on the background executor.
5. **A spawned server is never reaped** (`crates/client/src/lib.rs:906-934`). The app drops the `Child`. When that server exits, it stays a zombie until the app quits. Wait on it from a detached thread.
6. **The full snapshot is converted on the main thread** (`crates/ui/src/shell/workspace/events.rs:24-33`). `Issue::from_api` runs for every issue inside `apply_event`. Convert on the backend thread before the event reaches the workspace.

Add a test for each item where one fits.

## What I changed

Commit `6807a89`. Each item has a test.

1. The client reads a response's bytes straight into the target type. It parses `ErrorBody` only for status 400 and above. `raw` still returns a loose `Value` for the callers that want one.
2. `replace_all` drops the git panel, relations, reviews, sessions and the old-detail mark of every issue the new list lacks. Because of this, `load` no longer fetches an edited task that left the snapshot. The open task's normal fetch does it, so the request is not sent twice.
3. `WritePipeline` removes the sent key when the last write for that issue returns.
4. `DraftStore` sends each new file text to one writer thread, which writes and fsyncs it. A burst of changes writes once. `drafts::flush()` waits for queued writes. `DraftStore::open`, app quit, window close and the update restart call it. I used a plain thread, not the GPUI background executor, because `model` may not import GPUI.
5. `spawn_server` waits on the child from a detached thread, so a server that exits is reaped.
6. The API thread maps the snapshot to the app's catalog and issues. It sends a `Loaded` snapshot, so `apply_event` only stores it.
+++

tickets.title: App: the list, filter and sidebar allocate on every render and keystroke
tickets.description:
The issue list, the filter and the sidebar make many small allocations on each render or keystroke. Each one is small today, but the cost grows with the number of issues and labels.

+++ Agent notes
Found in the 2026-11-12 performance review. LLM-105 and LLM-112 fixed the large costs; these are what is left.

1. **Each visible row clones its issue and layout** (`crates/ui/src/issues/list.rs:1091`, `:1096-1097`). It also collects `tags` and `name_chars` into new `Vec`s and formats about five string element IDs (`:808`, `:853`, `:876`, `:1053`, `:1171`, `:1216`). Borrow the issue, share `Layout` through an `Rc`, and use tuple element IDs such as `("llm", id)`.
2. **The filter lowercases every title, key and label on each keystroke** (`crates/ui/src/issues/filter.rs:80`, `:240-248`). Keep lowercase copies on `Issue` at load, or use a case-insensitive search that does not allocate.
3. **Grouping walks all issues once per group** (`crates/ui/src/issues/rows.rs:156-227`). Unique values use linear search, and `Assignee::name()` builds a `SharedString` per comparison. Bucket each issue in one pass with a `HashMap`.
4. **"Hide old closed tasks" refilters on every update** (`list.rs:443`). Refilter only when `closed_before(cutoff)` changes for the updated issue, and start a timer for the next cutoff crossing.
5. **Background list builds are not combined** (`list.rs:334-367`). Above 2,000 issues, each update starts a full build, and a started build runs to the end even when a newer one replaces it. Run one build at a time, and one more at the end if something changed meanwhile.
6. **The sidebar counts every issue against every scope** (`crates/ui/src/shell/sidebar.rs:156-182`), and `render` clones the whole `Catalog` (`sidebar.rs:186`). Bucket issues by team, project, Trash and view in one pass. Borrow the catalog.

Measure items 1 to 3 with `perf_tests.rs` before and after, and put the numbers here.

## What I changed

Commit `aee36f2`.

1. Rows take a shared copy of their issue (`IssueStore::get_shared`), and share `Layout` through an `Rc`. `labels_that_fit` takes an iterator and allocates nothing, so the row no longer collects `name_chars`. The row builds only the tags that fit. The row's element IDs use `widgets::issue_part(name, id)`, a static name and the ID's low 64 bits, so they need no formatting. Tests find elements with the same call.
2. The text filter lowercases ASCII text into a buffer each thread keeps, then searches it. Non-ASCII text still goes through `to_lowercase`.
3. Grouping puts each issue in its groups in one pass, through a map per grouping. A test compares it with the old walk for every grouping and three sorts.
4. With "Hide old closed tasks" on, a change refilters only when it hides or shows the task, or moves its close time. The build reports when the next shown task gets old enough, and the list sets a timer for that moment.
5. One background build runs at a time. Calls meanwhile mark the rows stale. The result is then dropped, and one more build starts. A test checks that five keystrokes start two builds.
6. `ScopeCounts::of` counts every sidebar scope in one pass. The sidebar borrows the catalog instead of cloning it.

## Numbers

The machine ran other agents' builds, at a load average of 130, so the frame tests in `perf_tests.rs` were 3 to 10 times slower than the baseline, also on paths this change did not touch. I did not use them. Instead I timed the old and new code side by side in one process (`ab_times` in `issues/render_cost_tests.rs`, debug build, 10,000 issues, median):

| Step | Old | New |
|---|---|---|
| Group by status | 5.2 ms | 4.2 ms |
| Group by label | 11.9 ms | 6.1 ms |
| Group by assignee | 11.6 ms | 6.1 ms |

For the text match, a debug build favours the old code, because the standard library is prebuilt and optimized. A release build of both versions, 10,000 issues, gave 0.8 to 1.06 ms for the old match and 0.58 ms for the new one. Baseline before the change, sidebar open at 50,000 issues: 51 ms per frame.
+++

tickets.title: App: opening history downloads every description version and fetches the issue twice
tickets.description:
Opening a task's history downloads the full text of every version of its description. It also fetches the whole issue a second time and runs git again, only to read its sessions. A long-lived task with many versions sends hundreds of kilobytes each time.

+++ Agent notes


Found in the 2026-11-12 performance review.

## Cause

- `History` (`crates/ui/src/model/backend.rs:621-636`) calls `issue_history`, then `client.issue(&key)` and `with_commits` again, and keeps only `sessions`.
- When a live event hits the open task, `events.rs:36-44` calls `request_history`. The refresh just before did the same detail fetch and git run.
- The server returns every revision with its full body and no limit (`crates/server/src/ops/issues.rs:82`, `crates/server/src/store/revisions.rs:33`). Example: 80 versions of an 8 KB description is 640 KB per open.

## Fix

1. Return revision metadata in the history list. Fetch a revision body when the owner picks that version, or page the list.
2. Send the sessions with the open task's refresh, or give them their own endpoint, so `History` fetches only the history.
3. Do not refetch history on every live event for the open task. Refetch only when the event changed something history shows.
4. Update the CLI if it uses the same endpoint, and run `scripts/gen-agent-docs`.

This ticket builds on LLM-171, which changes how the open task is fetched.

## What I changed

Commit `e8ffc9e`.

- The issue and document history endpoints leave out each revision's text. `?bodies=true` brings it back. `Revision.body` is now optional.
- The CLI has `issue history --bodies` and `doc history --bodies`. I regenerated the agent docs.
- The app never needed the text: the Activity tab lists version numbers only. Restore by version still works through the CLI.
- Size estimate for 80 versions of 8 KB: before, about 640 KB per open. After, about 250 bytes per version, so about 20 KB. I estimated the per-version size from the JSON shape, not from a measured run.
- `History` in the app makes one request. It no longer fetches the issue or runs git. The sessions come with the open task's `IssueDetail`, and the store keeps them with the git panel.
- The app no longer asks for history on every issue event. The API thread sends the open task's history once after each live refresh that touched it. Every issue event shows in the Activity tab, so this is the only refetch it needs.
- Tests: the server leaves out bodies unless asked, the app's history has no bodies, sessions come with the detail, and a live event on the open task brings its history.
+++

tickets.title: Server: queries that do more work than they need
tickets.description:
Several server queries do more work than they need. None is slow at today's sizes, but each one grows with the data.

+++ Agent notes

Found in the 2026-11-12 performance review. The reviewer checked the plans with `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` on a fresh database.

1. **The snapshot uses 100-row pages** (`crates/server/src/store/issues.rs:662`). The client treats `limit` as a cap on the total (`crates/client/src/lib.rs:567`), so it cannot ask for bigger pages. Each page runs about 11 queries and reads all statuses and actors again. 3,000 issues need more than 30 round trips on every start and reconnect. Let `query_all` take a page size apart from the total, and use 1,000-row pages for the snapshot.
2. **The document list reads every body and drops it** (`crates/server/src/store/documents.rs:39`, `ops/documents.rs:35`). The app refetches the catalog on each document event. Use a list query without the body column.
3. **The default issue sort scans and sorts the whole table** (`store/issues.rs:371`): `SCAN i` and `USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY`. The CLI `issue list` and saved views use it. Add an expression index on the priority expression, `updated_at DESC` and `id`, filtered to `deleted_at IS NULL`.
4. **N+1 queries in team and project lists** (`crates/server/src/routes/teams.rs:16`, `routes/projects.rs:19`). They run on every catalog refresh. Load statuses, project teams and project repos in one query each.
5. **Two lookups scan whole tables.** `attachments WHERE url = ?` (`store/github.rs:20`) runs per pull request inside the GitHub poll. `activity WHERE entity_id = ?` (`store/activity.rs:95`) runs for document history, and activity rows are never deleted. Add indexes on `attachments (url)` and `activity (entity_id, seq)`.
6. **`actors::all` and `teams::statuses(None)` run several times per request**, three or more times in one issue detail load. Load them once per request and pass them down.

Check each change with `tests/perf.rs` at 50,000 issues.

### What I changed

Commit `6187f0a` on main.

1. `query_all` in the client now asks for pages of 1,000, the server's maximum, which is the new `MAX_ISSUE_PAGE` constant in api-types. `limit` still caps the total. I kept the API as it was, so no caller changed.
2. The document list and the document search now select an empty body. A document view still reads the body.
3. Migration 0013 adds `issues_default_sort`, an index on the priority expression, `updated_at DESC` and `id`, for rows that are not deleted. The plan is now `SCAN i USING INDEX issues_default_sort` with no temp sort. A page after a cursor uses a `SEARCH` on the same index. A unit test checks both plans, and it fails without the index. The index expression must match `SORT_PRIORITY`, and a comment in the migration says so.
4. The team list loads every status in one query. The project list loads its teams in one query and its repos in one query.
5. Migration 0013 also adds `attachments_url` and `activity_entity`. Both lookups now use `SEARCH`.
6. A new `issues::Lookup` holds the statuses and the actors. The issue detail loads it once and passes it to the issue, the children, the relations, the comments, the sessions and the reviews. Before, one detail read the statuses 3 times and the actors 3 times. Relations also ran the full issue loader for each related issue. That loader reads claims, blockers, costs and more, and a relation shows none of them. Relations now use the short-link query.

A new API test checks that each team and project in a list matches its own view. It also checks that the document list sends no body and that relations show the right short form.

**Numbers** from `tests/perf.rs` at 50,000 issues, release build. The machine load average was over 100 during these runs, because other agents were compiling. So the numbers are noisy, but each pair ran on the same machine.

| Measure | Without the change | With the change |
|---|---|---|
| Default sort, page of 100 | 16 ms, 54 ms | 1.7 ms, 3.3 ms |
| Default sort, page of 1,000 | 45 ms, 51 ms | 16 ms, 25 ms |
| Read all 50,000 issues in ID order | 500 pages of 100: 1.9 s to 11 s | 50 pages of 1,000: 1.1 s to 8.6 s |

The full read is the app's snapshot. In each run, pages of 1,000 took 25% to 60% less time than pages of 100, with 10 times fewer round trips.
+++

tickets.title: Server: write-lock waits, an idle GitHub poll write, and backup retries
tickets.description:
Three server background and write paths waste resources under load or after an error. A burst of agent writes can make app reads wait. The GitHub poll writes to the database every 5 minutes even when nothing changed. A failed backup retries a full copy every minute.

+++ Agent notes

Found in the 2026-11-12 performance review.

1. **Writers hold a pool connection while they wait for the write lock.** `state.rs:134` takes a read guard, then line 143 runs `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` on a pooled connection. The pool has 8 connections (`crates/server/src/db.rs:66`) and a 15-second busy timeout. Eight writes at once take every connection, and app reads wait. Make writers queue on a `tokio::sync::Mutex` before they take a connection, or give writes their own one-connection pool.
2. **The GitHub poll always commits** (`crates/server/src/github.rs:438`), and `state.rs:229` then increments `sync_dirty`. So the unpushed-writes count never stays at zero. Skip the commit and the dirty count when the poll changed nothing but its poll time.
3. **A failed backup retries every 60 seconds** (`crates/server/src/lib.rs:237`, `:243`). On a full disk, the server copies the whole database every minute. Back off after a failure, and delete the target file when `VACUUM INTO` fails. Check whether a failed copy can leave a partial file that later counts as a valid backup.

Add a test for each item.

### What I changed

Commit `d2f75ee` on main.

1. `Write::begin` now waits on a new `write_queue` mutex before it takes a connection. The queue is released right after the commit, before live events go out. A test holds one write open, starts 12 more, and checks that a read still gets a connection at once. The test fails without the queue.
2. The poll counts changed rows with SQLite's `total_changes()`. When only the poll time changed, the commit skips the `sync_dirty` bump. I kept the poll-time commit, so the next commit walk stays short. An attachment update now skips rows where the title and metadata already match, so a PR read again counts as no change. The GitHub test checks that an idle poll leaves `sync_dirty` as it was.
3. A failed daily backup now doubles the pause after each failure in a row: 2 minutes, then 4, up to 6 hours. A success resets it to 1 minute. The copy is written under a `.partial` name and renamed when whole. A failed `VACUUM INTO` deletes its target and journal file. The newest-daily-backup check counts only `.db` files. A partial file could count as a valid backup before this fix, which stopped retries for a day. Tests cover the delay values and the cleanup.
+++

tickets.title: Mascot: clicks startle the sleeping cat, and it jumps up to sit
tickets.description:
Clicks wake the sleeping cat with a startle.

1. The cat sleeps. A first click jolts it awake: its head snaps up with wide eyes.
2. A second click within 1 second makes it jump up and land sitting. Then it watches, as it does today after a click.
3. With no second click, it falls back asleep after 1 second.
4. For the next 3 seconds, a click startles it at once: it jolts and jumps in one go, and lands sitting.

The art is done. Try the rules in `design/mascot/preview.html`, mode "Try it: click the cat".

+++ Agent notes
The owner asked for this on 2026-11-12. The art is in `design/mascot/sprites.js` (commit `5833b59`): `startle` (the whole thing), `jolt` (one frame, 1000 ms) and `jump` (the rest of `startle`). The preview's "click" mode in `preview.html` (`tapTo`, `tapTick`) shows the exact rules.

## Plan

1. Run `node design/mascot/export.mjs --app` and commit `crates/ui/assets/mascot/mascot.json`. Check that the new `H` shadow colour comes through in both palettes.
2. Add `AnimId::Jolt`, `AnimId::Jump` and `AnimId::Startle` in `crates/ui/src/shell/mascot/sprites.rs`.
3. In `behaviour.rs`, add acts for the jolt and the jump. The jolt timeline is one 1000 ms step, so its `advance` is the "no second click" timeout. It goes back to `Sleep` and starts a 3 s drowsy window. Sleep steps count the window down.
4. `click` on `Sleep` or `Nap`: in the drowsy window, play `Startle`; otherwise `Jolt`. A click during `Jolt` plays `Jump`. Clicks during `Jump` or `Startle` do nothing. When the jump or startle ends, start `Watch`, with the same follow-up as a click wake today.
5. `set_active(true)` during a jolt goes to work, as `Sleep` does. A jump or startle plays to the end first.

## A choice I made

Today a hover on a sleeping cat makes it sit and watch. The pointer always hovers before it clicks, so that rule would wake the cat before any click. From now on, a hover does not wake a sleeping or napping cat. Hover still keeps an awake, watching cat sitting. Update the behaviour notes at the top of `behaviour.rs` and the mascot memory rules to match.

## Tests

Add behaviour tests for each rule: jolt then jump, jolt then timeout back to sleep, a click in the 3 s window plays the startle, a click after the window jolts again, hover does not wake, and an agent start during a jolt.

`crates/ui/src/shell/mascot/mod.rs` is being changed by LLM-169 (the cat's timer) in parallel. Keep changes there small, and rebase often.

## What I changed

Commit `d42ac41`, landed on main. My soft reset in that commit also undid LLM-172's `backend.rs` and `live_tests.rs`. I restored both exactly in `ec535c7`.

- `export.mjs --app` now writes `RULES` into `mascot.json`. `sprites.rs` reads `joltMs`, `joltLockMs` and `drowsyMs` into `Rules`. Rust has no copies of these times.
- The jolt is two steps of the one jolt frame: the lock (400 ms) and the rest (800 ms). Clicks in the lock do nothing. A click in the second step plays `Jump`.
- The jump and the startle both end on the first watch frame, so the watch starts at step 0, not at the happy eyes. Then it walks or naps, as after any click.
- An agent start during a jump or startle does not cut it short. The cat then watches, as a watching cat does today.
- A click on a watching cat still shows the happy eyes.
- `set_hovered` no longer returns a value: a hover never changes the act now.
- Tests: 10 new or rewritten behaviour and view tests. `cargo test -p llmtodo-ui` passes. One full run under load failed `hover_and_clicks_do_nothing_during_the_walk_in` once ("not visible"). It passed alone and in four more full runs.
+++

+++ Timing change
The owner changed the timing on 2026-11-12, in commit `3ff82b9`. Time moves the cat on, not the number of clicks.

- The jolt now lasts `RULES.joltMs`, 1200 ms.
- Clicks in the first `RULES.joltLockMs`, 400 ms, of the jolt do nothing. So a fast double click no longer jumps at once.
- A click after that, and before the jolt ends, makes it jump.
- The drowsy window is `RULES.drowsyMs`, 3000 ms.

Read the times from `RULES` (export them into `mascot.json`), not from constants in Rust.
+++

+++ Review
### Steps to reproduce
1. Open the app with no agent at work. The cat sleeps.
2. Move the mouse onto the cat.
3. Click the cat once.
4. Wait half a second, then click again.
5. Wait for it to sleep again. Double click it fast.
6. Wait until it dozes off. Click it within 3 seconds.

### What to check
- The cat keeps sleeping.
- Its head snaps up with wide eyes.
- It jumps up and lands sitting, then watches.
- It only jolts. It does not jump.
- It jolts and jumps in one go, and lands sitting.
+++

tickets.description:
Add optional animations to the app. A switch in Settings turns them on. They are off by default.

## What I built (3b5391e)

- `crates/ui/src/shell/motion.rs` holds every helper. A global holds the switch. Off, each helper returns the plain element, so the app is as before.
- Settings has an Animations row. It saves to `ui.json` as `animations`, default false.
- Hover, press and selection fills fade on list rows and sidebar rows. A fill that turns on shows at once or in 60 ms. A fill that goes away fades over 170 ms. A press shows at the moment of the click.
- The palette, the help overlay, the new-task dialog and the claims list fade in and drop 6 px into place, in 150 ms.
- Tooltips fade in over 110 ms.
- The sidebar's column grows and shrinks over 220 ms when it opens and closes (48c8163). The list or Settings beside it moves with it, and the panel rides the column's edge. The task view slides in 1.5 rem from the right and fades in (89ff27e). The views draw again only during those frames.

- Opening a group sends a wave down its rows (cdb0aa7). Each row fades in and drops 8 px. The front slows down toward the bottom and spreads over 40 rows, so nothing jumps at the end. Its clock starts at the first frame after the click.
- Closing a group keeps its rows under the header for 180 ms. The rows below slide up over them, so the group crops from the bottom.
- A new sort or grouping sends a quick wave down the visible rows. Each row fades in and rises 4 px.
- The group chevron turns between closed and open over 180 ms. Group headers fade their hover like task rows.
- A newly picked tab's content fades in and rises 4 px. Moving to another task on the same tab does not replay it.
- The animations follow the system's Reduce motion setting. Settings still saves the switch as the owner set it.

## What I left out

- GPUI Kit buttons and switches. Their hover and press styles are inside the kit, so a fade needs a fork. The kit Switch already moves its thumb with a spring.
- Closing animations. GPUI drops an element at once when it leaves the tree, so an exit fade needs each view to keep a closing state. I left it out to keep the change small.
- No GPUI element can scale, so overlays fade and drop instead of growing.
- The sidebar's width animation lays out the list again on each of its frames. It runs only while the sidebar opens or closes.

tickets.title: Order of sub-issues: server and CLI
tickets.description:
Steps on an epic's sub-issues, stored as order edges. `issue order set|show|clear`, `--order-step`, skill text. See the plan in LLM-206.

+++ Agent notes

Landed in `6351093` on main.

**What I built**

- Migration 0014 adds `issues.order_step`, `relations.source` (`manual` or `order`) and an index on `(parent_id, order_step)`.
- `Issue.order_step` and `Relation.source` are in api-types. `GET` and `PUT /v1/issues/{key}/order` read and write the whole order. `UpdateIssue.order_step` moves one task.
- `ops/order.rs` holds the rules. Each order change rewrites the parent's order edges in the same transaction. A new parent, a trash and a restore rewrite them too.
- Each edge is checked against the other `blocks` edges. A cycle fails with exit 6 and `details.reason = order_cycle`, and nothing is written.
- A manual relation on the same two tasks takes over an order edge. `relation remove` refuses an order edge and points to `--order-step none`.
- One order change writes one `order` activity event on the parent, with the old and new steps as keys. Order edges write no relation events.
- CLI: `issue order set|show|clear`, and `issue update --order-step <n|none>`. Bare numbers take the parent's team.
- Docs: "Order an epic" in the skill guide, a line in SKILL.md, a SPEC section and decision 49. I regenerated `cli-reference.md`.

**Checks**

- Tests cover set and show, a group step, the frontier, depth, a cycle with a manual edge, trash and restore, a parent change, foreign keys and repeats. The CLI test covers bare numbers, `--order-step` and clear.
- fmt, clippy and the full workspace tests pass, with 526 app tests.
- The 50,000-issue perf test passes. A page of 1,000 issues on 47,500 chained edges takes 51 ms. The edge queries did not change.
- I ran `scripts/publish` and restarted the server, so the live tracker runs schema 14.

**For LLM-208 and LLM-209**

- The app does not react to the `order` event yet. It should reload the parent's sub-issues, then their depth and open blockers.
- Order edges get new relation IDs on each rewrite.
- A trashed task loses its step for good, so a restore does not put it back.
+++

tickets.title: Order of sub-issues: group by Parent and the order line
tickets.description:
Group by Parent in the task list. A narrow column draws a vertical line with one dot per step. See the plan in LLM-206.

+++ Agent notes

Landed in `428d2d7` on main.

**What I built**

- `GroupBy::Parent`: `:group parent`, the Group menu and the saved setting. One group per parent in key order, then "No parent". The header shows the parent's key and title.
- Inside a group, tasks with a step come first, by step. Each step keeps the chosen sort, also when it is reversed. Tasks with no step follow.
- `Column::Order`, 1.25 rem, left of the status. It shows only under this grouping and hides at narrow widths after Waiting and before Deps. Each row draws two line halves and maybe a dot, inside the row's own height.
- A dot is filled when every live task of the step is done or canceled. Tasks that the filter or scope hides still count.
- A drop on a parent header, or on a task in a parent group, sets the parent. A drop on "No parent" clears it. Marked tasks move together.
- The task view shows order edges as one chip each way, "Order: step N of KEY". A click opens the parent. `:undepend` and `:unblock` on an order edge say to use `:step none`.
- Live: the `order` event on a parent makes the app fetch the parent's sub-issues by `parent` filter. Each one refreshes like a touched issue, and the tasks that wait for it follow.
- `scripts/seed-demo`: the epic "Onboarding flow" with seven tasks in five steps. Step 1 is done, step 2 holds three tasks. An eighth task has no step, to show the rows after the line.
- SPEC "Order (LLM-206)" lists the app rules.

**Checks**

- New tests: row building, the dot and line rules, a reversed sort, a filter, a collapsed group, the column in the window, keys across groups, drops on headers, the order chips and the live event. The live test fails without the new event code.
- The column width tests now pass the order column as hidden, plus a new test for its own hide rank.
- `render_cost_tests.rs` and the scroll tests pass. fmt, clippy and the workspace tests pass.

**Left open**

- A restore of a trashed task cannot keep its step in the app alone. The server clears the step on trash and renumbers the others, so the app knows neither the old step nor its place after a renumber. A task trashed from the CLI, or in an earlier app run, has no trace in the app. The fix belongs on the server: keep the step of a trashed task in a separate column, such as `trashed_order_step` with the keys of its step mates, and put it back on restore when those tasks still share a step. Otherwise add it as a new last step.

**Rework: step numbers in the dots**

Landed in `805c9ae` on main, from the owner feedback below.

- When a parent has more than one step, each dot shows its step number. One step keeps the small plain dot.
- The step count comes from every live sub-issue, so a filter that hides steps does not drop the numbers.
- The numbered dot is 14 px, enough for two digits. The row stays 28 px high, because the dot is drawn on top of the line.
- The number takes the colour the dot is not filled with. A filled dot gets the page colour, and a hollow dot gets the muted text colour. Both pairs have the contrast of muted text on the page, in every theme.
- Tests: the marks carry the numbers, a single step has no number, and the window test finds the number inside its dot and the dot inside its row.

+++

tickets.title: Order of sub-issues: palette commands to change the order
tickets.description:
Palette commands `:step <n>`, `:step new`, `:step none` move the selected tasks between steps. See the plan in LLM-206.

+++ Agent notes

Landed in `722df1e` on main.

**What I built**

- `:step <n>`, `:step new` and `:step none`. They act on the marked tasks, or on the selected or open task.
- `model/order.rs` holds the rules with no GPUI: it reads the parent's steps from the store and works out the whole new order. A step number means the step as the list shows it before the move. Empty steps drop out.
- The app sends one `Write::SetOrder` on the parent, through `PUT /issues/{key}/order`. Marked tasks land in one step together. Single `--order-step` writes would make one new step per task.
- The rows change at once. The live `order` event then brings the server's steps, depths and open blockers. A failed write refreshes the parent and every task in the order, which undoes the early change.
- Errors change nothing and say why in the status bar: no parent, different parents, a step past the new last one, a bad argument, and a locked task. The palette shows every command's result in the status bar, so `:step` does the same.
- The same step again says "nothing changed" and sends no write.
- The palette suggests `step new`, `step none` and `step 1`, and the help lists `:step 2`.

**Checks**

- Unit tests for the parse and the move rules. Window tests for one task, marked tasks, every error, and the palette picking the first match. A live test sends the write through the backend to a real server and sees the steps come back.
- fmt, clippy and the workspace tests pass.
+++

tickets.title: App: Hide after 0 always hides Done tasks, except in open chains
tickets.description:
The Settings field "Hide after" takes 0. With 0, the list hides every Done and Canceled task at once, whatever its age.

One exception, for every value of Hide after: a closed task stays visible while an open task still depends on it, directly or through other tasks. Steps in an epic's order are such a chain, because order edges are blocks relations. So the done steps of an ordered epic stay on screen while later steps are open. When every task in the chain is closed, the chain hides like any other closed task.

+++ Agent notes
Landed on main in b76287e.

- The server sends `has_open_dependents` on every issue. It is true on a closed, live task that an open, live task waits for, directly or through closed tasks. One more recursive query per list page computes it.
- `issue query --closed-blockers-of <KEY>` lists the closed tasks that KEY waits for through closed tasks. The app's live refresh asks for them next to `--depends-on`, so the flag follows a close, reopen, trash or relation change.
- "Hide after" takes 0 to 3650. 0 hides every closed task at once, also one with no close time. A held task sets no hide timer.
- Perf on 50,000 issues: a snapshot over one closed chain of 49,000 tasks takes 16 s. The existing depth walk takes 31 s over one open chain, so this field adds no worse case. Normal shapes stay in milliseconds.
- Tests: `closed_issues_held_by_open_dependents` (server), `issues::hide_tests`, `zero_days_saves_and_hides_a_task_closed_just_now`, `closing_the_last_step_refreshes_the_closed_steps_before_it_live`.
+++

+++ Review
### Steps to reproduce
1. Open Settings.
2. Turn on Hide old closed tasks.
3. Type 0 in Hide after.
4. Open All issues.
5. Find an epic with an order where some steps are done and later steps are open.
6. Close the last open step of that epic.
7. Open that step again.

### What to check
- The line under Hide after says 0 hides closed tasks at once.
- Closed tasks that no open task waits for are gone from the list.

tickets.title: Server: depth and open dependents stay fast on long chains
tickets.description:
Reading every issue is slow when tasks form one long chain. The server computes `depth` and `has_open_dependents` again on every read.

Measured by LLM-214 on 50,000 issues:
- One open chain of 49,000 tasks: depth takes 31 s.
- One closed chain of 49,000 tasks: `has_open_dependents` takes 16 s.
- Normal data loads in milliseconds.

Goal: both cases load in under 200 ms, and normal data stays as fast as today.

+++ Agent notes

**Landed in 2772539.** I did not store the values in columns. The server keeps the whole dependency graph in memory instead, and builds it again only after a write that changes it.

**Profile.** The two recursive queries took nearly all of the time. Each page walked the whole chain again. On one open chain of 49,000 tasks, depth took 460 ms of a 485 ms page. On one closed chain, `has_open_dependents` took 250 to 310 ms of a 270 ms page.

**Fix.**
- The server reads every `blocks` edge and the live issues on them, and computes depth and `has_open_dependents` for every issue in Rust. Each issue and edge is visited once.
- Migration 0016 adds `dep_graph_token`, one random token. Triggers replace it when a `blocks` relation changes, an issue's status or trash time changes, an issue is deleted, or a status type changes. A read with a new token builds the graph again.
- Both build queries return one string through `group_concat`. sqlx hands over rows one at a time: 100,000 edges took 100 ms as rows and 15 ms as one string. Up to 5,000 issues on edges, the build looks them up by ID. Above that, it scans every live issue, because 50,000 lookups by ID took 130 ms and a scan took 20 ms.

**Measured** on 50,000 issues, release build, machine load average 32:

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Page of 1000, one open chain | 485 ms | 50 ms |
| Page of 1000, one closed chain | 270 ms | 45 ms |
| A status change that builds the graph again | none | 75 ms |
| Every page in ID order, open chain | 13.5 s | 2.0 s |
| Every page in ID order, closed chain | 7.9 s | 1.5 s |

Normal data did not change: a page of 1000 with no relations takes 35 ms, as before. Dependency work now costs about 6 ms of each page. Reading every page in the chain cases still takes about 2 s, because the test adds usage data to every issue first.

**Tests.** The perf test now fails above 200 ms for a page and for a write on each chain case. A new API test checks that the next read follows each kind of write: relation add, relation remove, close, reopen, trash and restore.

**Left open.**
- `--depends-on` and `--closed-blockers-of` still walk with recursive queries. The app runs them after each live event. I did not time them. They use the same kind of walk that took half a second per page on a 49,000-task chain. They could read the in-memory graph next.
- The live event does not carry the changed tasks, so the app still needs those refresh queries.
+++

tickets.title: Server: the live refresh queries read the in-memory dependency graph
tickets.description:
LLM-216 keeps the dependency graph in memory for depth and open dependents. The app still runs issue query --depends-on and --closed-blockers-of after each live event, and both use recursive SQL. On a long chain they likely take about half a second each.

Make both filters read the in-memory graph. Better still, send the tasks whose depth or open dependents changed in the live event itself, so the app needs no refresh query. Keep the CLI filters. Add perf tests on the 49,000-task chain cases from LLM-216.

+++ Agent notes

Both filters now walk the in-memory graph. A trashed start issue reads its direct edges with one plain query.

Perf on the 49,000-task chain, old SQL against the graph:

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| depends_on near the end, 10 tasks | 1.2 ms | 1.4 ms |
| depends_on the head, 49,998 tasks | 9.3 s | 3.3 to 5.1 s |
| closed_blockers_of, 48,999 tasks | 10.6 s | 3.4 to 3.9 s |
| closed_blockers_of near the head, 1 task | 2.0 ms | 0.8 ms |

The old SQL was already fast when a chain reaches few tasks. The ticket's half-second guess holds only for long reaches. The remaining time on long reaches is paging 49,000 rows.

Not done: sending changed tasks inside the live event, so the app skips the refresh query. It changes the event format and the app's refresh logic. It fits a separate ticket.
+++
